DISGATE101: Programming enables implementation,testing andexplanation of computational economic andfinancial models; actual structuredPython anddata collections are the complementary method,not a guaranteed finance project.
DISMATH211: Linear systems,matrixmethods,least-squares,eigenvalues,quadraticforms andSVD support multivariable economic/financial models andstatisticalestimation. Complementary mathematical foundations,not a specialisedfinance syllabus.
DISMATH213: Numerical roots,quadrature,differentialequations andlinear/nonlinear systems,error/stability analysis supply concrete solution/validation methods for quantitative economic models. Financial applications are not claimed as prescribed coursework.
DISARIN211: Probability,Bayesian inference,expectedutility,temporalmodels,Markovdecisionprocesses andbandits develop formal decisions underuncertainty,complementing financialrisk/economicchoice; intelligentagent rather than finance setting.
DISARIN311: Actual heuristic/local/global optimisation,first/secondorder methods,linear/discrete optimisation andimplementation support constrained quantitative decision models. Complementary computational methods,not dedicatedportfolio theory.
DISCOMP312: Matrix/Fourier computation,greedy/dynamicprogramming andnetworkflows plus experimental algorithm evaluation support efficient quantitative modelimplementation. Broad algorithms remain complementary to economic/financial inquiry,not a replacement for finance theory.
